newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia bank sells HRK 80.5 mln bills, rates ease.
newsitem.headline: Croatia bank sells HRK 80.5 mln bills, rates ease.

text.p: Croatia's central bank sold 80.5 million kuna worth of five- and 13-week liquidity bills at a regular auction, with rates resuming a downward trend.
The rates eased again after inching up last Wednesday for the first time in weeks to restart their downward path.
The five-week rate eased to 7.95 from 8.0 percent as the bank accepted 74.5 out of 75.5 million kuna bids.
It also sold commercial banks six million kuna of 13-week paper at an average 9.83 percent, down 17 basis points.
There were no bids for 26-week bills, which were last issued at 17.50 percent in July. Full details avaiable on page NBHT.
The National Bank of Croatia will drain a total 191.7 million kuna from the banking system this week through reserve payment at a new higher ratio of 32.8 instead of 30.8 percent.
It will repay banks 170.8 million kuna that had been tied up in bills under a former mandatory subscription, which has been scrapped from September.
